issues.problem: The requirement says the prod image SHALL bake the internal API origin http://api:3001 for Next rewrites, but the prescribed build arg is API_URL: ${API_URL:-http://api:3001}. Docker Compose will use any API_URL from the operator shell/.env, so a common dev/staging value such as http://localhost:3002 or http://api:3002 can still be baked into routes-manifest.json and preserve the production rewrite failure this change is meant to eliminate.
issues.fix: Do not reuse the generic API_URL interpolation for the prod build arg; hardcode API_URL: http://api:3001 in docker-compose.prod.yml or introduce a dedicated required internal-build var with validation/documentation that it must be the Docker-network API origin.

issues.problem: The revised CAS plan stops the row update but still leaves the existing publishAuto success path ambiguous: PublicationService.publishAuto unconditionally increments publish metrics and enqueues ingestion after saveAssembledReport returns (apps/api/src/modules/publication/publication.service.ts:242-267), and AutoPublisherScheduler unconditionally counts missing sections, emits periodAutoPublish audit, and adds the id after publishAuto returns (apps/api/src/modules/period/auto-publisher.scheduler.ts:92-111). Because AssembledReport does not expose archived/periodState (packages/shared/src/schemas/report.schema.ts:59-70; apps/api/src/modules/published-report-snapshot.ts:55-66), a zero-row guarded update that simply re-reads/returns the current archived draft can be misreported as a successful auto-publish even though the spec says it was skipped.
issues.fix: Specify and test an explicit skipped outcome from the auto path (repository/service/scheduler) so CAS zero-row matches do not emit publish metrics, ingestion, audit, missing-section counts, or periodIds.

issues.problem: The design says the new head lifecycle target should match the head weekly-report page resolver by using getCurrentEditableId, but the actual non-viewer default path still uses getActiveReportId, which has a published fallback, no archived filter, and different ordering. A head on the main weekly report page can therefore receive one reportId from weeklyReport.get and then be rejected by period.publish/reopen because the lifecycle authz resolver chooses a different target.
issues.fix: Either align the head/default weeklyReport.get resolver with the proposed lifecycle resolver and cover that behavior, or make the lifecycle authz resolver match the actual UI target and update the delta/specs accordingly.

issues.problem: The single-lead dispatch design says to prove scope by resolving the lead's ReportSection on that report, but the spec also requires an in-scope lead with no section yet to return no-matching-section. issues.problem: The plan filters listExecutions recipients after the existing service/repository pagination, but RemindersService paginates before return (apps/api/src/modules/reminders/reminders.service.ts:230-241) over the repository's unscoped newest-100 slice (apps/api/src/modules/reminders/reminders.prisma-repository.ts:290-295). issues.fix: Filter to the caller-visible recipient set before pagination/cursor calculation, or move the recipient predicate into the execution query and paginate the scoped set.

issues.problem: The DB-resolved publish target is specified as the same query review.dashboard currently uses: periodStatus in open/reopened and periodStart <= now. That query omits archived:false and a deterministic id desc tiebreak, while the durable current-editable contract and repository implementation define the current editable period as non-archived and ordered by periodStart desc, id desc. Because period uniqueness is explicitly a non-goal, two matching rows or an archived-open row can make dashboard/assembledReport/publish pick an arbitrary or archived period, reintroducing a stale/wrong publish target under the new path.
issues.fix: Specify and test a shared current-editable resolver/query for review.dashboard, review.assembledReport, and review.publish: periodStatus in open/reopened, periodStart <= now, archived:false, orderBy periodStart desc then id desc.

issues.problem: The atomicity plan wraps only the five named upsert phases, but current saveSnapshot also calls ensureFallbackReportingGroup between group and user phases; that helper performs a reportingGroup.upsert (apps/api/src/modules/admin/admin-snapshot-write.queries.ts:282, apps/api/src/modules/admin/admin-group.queries.ts:29), so leaving it outside the transaction can still commit a default group before a later user/project/period/rule failure, contradicting the spec's 'database matches its pre-call state' requirement.
issues.fix: Require ensureFallbackReportingGroup/current snapshot write setup that can write DB rows to run inside the same transaction, and widen its client type like the upsert helpers.

issues.problem: The scheduled-to-open recovery is internally wrong for one of the cases it explicitly names: if two scheduled rows with the same boundary are flipped by the same updateMany, the new partial unique index can reject the statement even though no open row exists yet; treating that P2002 as 'already-open' would leave the boundary with no opened period and silently skip the lifecycle transition. Current code uses one bulk updateMany for all due scheduled rows at apps/api/src/modules/period/period-creator.scheduler.ts:83, and the spec only covers the simpler case where an open row already exists at openspec/changes/period-uniqueness-db-constraint/specs/period-uniqueness-constraint/spec.md:107.
issues.fix: Change the scheduled-to-open plan to update due scheduled rows per boundary/row and, on P2002, re-read for an existing open row; if none exists, deterministically open one scheduled row and leave/report the duplicates instead of blanket-skipping.

issues.problem: The tasks require implementing a P2002 guard for the scheduler scheduled-to-open updateMany at tasks.md:49, and the spec has a dedicated scheduled-to-open collision scenario at spec.md:107, but the test list only covers scheduler report.create plus reopen/unarchive; there is no task that proves the scheduled-to-open catch works or catches the no-open duplicate-scheduled case above.
issues.fix: Add a scheduler scheduled-to-open test that forces P2002 on the due scheduled flip, verifies the intended recovery, and verifies non-P2002 failures still propagate.

issues.problem: The revised gate is still only specified as viewer/author non-archived co-ownership, but current leadForm.byPeriod is just a protected procedure that passes arbitrary reportId/authorId to getByPeriod, and getByPeriod currently resolves a foreign section from requestedAuthorId after hasSharedProduct without first proving the caller has their own section/access in that report (apps/api/src/infrastructure/trpc/trpc.router.ts:2099-2113; apps/api/src/modules/report-sections/lead-form.service.ts:168-179). The sibling getCrossAuthorContent path the proposal cites does have that report-access precheck before returning foreign content (apps/api/src/modules/report-sections/lead-form.service.ts:256-264). As written, the change can still allow a lead who currently co-owns a product with the author to read that author's section for a report/period the caller does not belong to, only now filtered to shared products.
issues.fix: Require and test a caller-owned/access-granting section in the requested report before any lead cross-author getByPeriod read, matching getCrossAuthorContent's ownSection precheck; otherwise fall back/deny without reading the foreign section.

issues.problem: The proposal types the service-level fillFrom source-missing check, but the actual copy path still has a bare `throw new Error` when `fillFromSection` re-reads the source. issues.fix: Include `lead-form.prisma-repository.ts` in scope and throw `LeadFormDomainError` for the repository source-missing guard, or otherwise make the copy path preserve NOT_FOUND under the race.
